items.title: Parents of Australian facing possible death penalty in Syria question confession
items.description: The family of a Gold Coast man who has been charged with murder over the death of an Australian in Syria is frustrated by the lack of progress made by the federal government in the case.

items.title: 'Take them seriously': CFMEU administrator on Setka threats
items.description: CFMEU administrator Michael Crosby has opened up on threats from John Setka, cast doubt on a statement made by former Victorian premier Jacinta Allan and questioned the value of royal commissions.

items.title: Opposition senators say 'PM must act today' on Labor MP charged with assault
items.description: Federal Labor MP Luke Gosling has been charged with assaulting NT Administrator David Connolly, the territory equivalent of a state governor, at a festival earlier this month.

items.title: Pilbara traditional owners set to appeal Fortescue's $150m native title penalty
items.description: Yindjibarndi native title holders have voted to continue their decades-long legal battle with mining billionaire Andrew Forrest.

items.title: 'Sadness' falls across coastal community after double murder-suicide
items.description: Volunteers from a regional SA town answered the call when the alarm was raised to search for a missing mother and her children.

items.title: Live: Aussies win first cycling gold with stunning team pursuit triumph
items.description: Australia's women's team pursuit cycling squad claims their nation's first gold on the track, surging late to set a new Games record at the velodrome. Follow live.

items.title: 'Try not to die': Why Glasgow's gales hit different for hurdlers
items.description: Australian hurdler Michelle Jenneke says she is jealous of her sprint compatriots who get to enjoy tailwinds, while she fears for her life when she feels a gale at her back.

items.title: Nauru officially changes name to Naoero
items.description: Nauru has officially changed its name to Naoero, the government has announced.

items.title: FIFA wants to sell the World Cup to a Trump associate. Here's what we know
items.description: Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in FIFA's events and competitions arm to investors would grant them control over the World Cup and has drawn condemnation from the organising confederations.

items.title: Cats hold off Magpies comeback for critical MCG win
items.description: Geelong bursts out of the gates and then holds off Collingwood's fightback for a critical 25-point win at the MCG.

items.title: Roosters put up 82 points for highest NRL score in 91 years
items.description: The Roosters have scored the third-most points ever seen in Australian rugby league first grade match and beaten the clock against a hapless North Queensland side.

items.title: A turbulent week in Victorian politics has Canberra on high alert
items.description: With a new premier installed in Victoria there are questions about what the state's electoral situation could mean federally, for all parties.

items.title: US strikes 'dozens of targets' in Iran as war threatens to engulf Middle East
items.description: America's military strikes "dozens" of Revolutionary Guard targets across Iran, as the spread of hostilities to Egypt, Iraq and Saudi Arabia threatens to plunge the rest of the Middle East into all-out conflict.

items.title: Why China's memory chips could help end 'RAMageddon'
items.description: China's leading memory chip maker CXMT is emerging as a potential alternative source of memory for a market under strain from the AI boom, observers say.

items.title: 'My body is your worst nightmare': Loving your body in the GLP-1 era
items.description: Body acceptance in a era when social media is awash with before-and-after weight-loss content and aggressive marketing from companies selling GLP-1 drugs can be hard. But these experts have some tips.

items.title: Silent discos are drawing in crowds across Australia
items.description: Silent disco participants could all be listening to different music in their soundproof headphones, but the joy of dancing unites them as one.

items.title: Two-decade-old Toyota Corolla stuns Gibb River Road onlookers
items.description: Jonny Charles is venturing across the famous Kimberley four-wheel-drive track in a 2002 Toyota Corolla, selling coffees out of his boot to fund the trip.

items.title: See how the price of everything has changed with inflation
items.description: The good news this week is inflation has eased slightly. The bad news is it remains stubbornly high. So we've tracked how the prices of everyday items have changed.

items.title: Neptune's moon system is bizarre. JWST data helps explain why
items.description: Neptune's strange moon and ring system has puzzled astronomers for decades, but data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) might help explain how it formed.

items.title: Teacher used laptop decorated with a 'free Palestine' sticker, inquiry told
items.description: Antisemitism in schools and against young people has been a key focus of the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion in Sydney today.

items.title: Online watchdog takes Telegram to court over terrorism videos
items.description: The Office of the eSafety Commissioner will allege Telegram neglected its legal obligations when it allowed videos, including of the Christchurch mosque massacre, to remain on the platform.

items.title: Gina Rinehart lobbied Qld government to move Olympic events to Rockhampton
items.description: A letter from Ms Rinehart to Jarrod Bleijie, obtained under right to information laws, asked the government to consider Rockhampton before the LNP's Games Delivery plan release in March 2025.

items.title: People across Ireland wake up at all hours to watch AFLW
items.description: These Irish families get up at all hours of the night to watch AFLW and host viewing parties with 30-plus people for big games.

items.title: 'Didn't think the law applied to us': NSW Reformers in spotlight at ICAC
items.description: Robert Assaf, co-founder of the NSW Reformers, has fronted a corruption inquiry for the fourth day of hearings.

items.title: Cricketer dubbed 'Clicky Ponting' suspended as stats show unusual trend
items.description: The club at the centre of the '"Clicky Ponting" amateur cricket scandal suspends the player allegedly involved as data shows dramatic increases in catches when he played.
